clue.text: It's a mistake to make frightening noise repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us to say the noise more than once, here twice

parts.note: boo is the noise made to startle someone

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for shouting to scare people over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A boo-boo is an informal word for a silly blunder or slip.

clue.text: Having courage to confront a strong type?

parts.note: bold means brave, having courage
to face is to confront

explanation.surface: Bravery is needed to stand up to a tough character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strong type' is a printing typeface, not a tough person.
explanation.definitionFit: Boldface is heavy printing type, so it is a strong typeface.

clue.text: Award for film, so scary it can't be shown in full

indicators.text: it can't be shown in full
indicators.note: not shown in full means only an inner run of the words is used

explanation.surface: A horror film too frightening to screen uncut wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first and last letters of SO SCARY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the Academy Award statuette given for achievement in cinema.

clue.text: Sick leave

explanation.surface: A note about sick leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Off means unwell, feeling off, and also to go away, as in be off.

clue.text: Country girl left university, having got first

indicators.note: the girl has the other pieces placed in front of her, so she comes last

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A rural lass quits her studies after graduating top of her year.
explanation.definitionFit: Portugal is a nation on the Iberian peninsula, an example of a country.

clue.text: It should have been paid long ago in coppers

definitions.text: It should have been paid long ago

explanation.surface: A debt long overdue is settled in small change.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD BILL is British slang for the police; 'coppers' looks like pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: An old bill is one overdue, and the Old Bill is slang for police officers.

clue.text: Having no idea how inconsiderate one might be

explanation.surface: Someone is unaware how unkind they can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughtless literally means lacking thought, and in use means careless of others' feelings.

clue.text: High speed gear oil of a sort

indicators.note: high means drunk or intoxicated, so the letters reel into another order

explanation.surface: A car's top gear and some lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeseed oil is pressed from grape pips, one kind of cooking oil.

clue.text: Permit given to pilot to attack?

parts.note: to let is to permit
to fly is to pilot an aircraft

explanation.surface: A pilot is given clearance to launch a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To let fly is an idiom for launching a verbal or physical attack.

clue.text: First person in France set over church translator

indicators.note: in a down clue, set over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: je is French for I, the first person singular
Rome stands for the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: A Frenchman placed above a church official to translate.
explanation.definitionFit: St Jerome translated the Bible into Latin, producing the Vulgate.

clue.text: Pounds I filched dishonestly in the city

parts.note: L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

indicators.note: something done dishonestly is crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pockets cash by theft somewhere in town.
explanation.walkthrough: L, I and FILCHED are rearranged together. LICHFIELD is a cathedral city in Staffordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lichfield is an English cathedral city, so it is an instance of a city.

clue.text: Style of painting that's the norm in some books

indicators.note: in tells us the norm sits inside the books

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
par is the standard or normal level

explanation.surface: An art style is described as the usual thing in certain volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s movement of abstract painting using optical illusions.

clue.text: Shortly expected to be open

explanation.surface: Something due soon will be candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthcoming means both about to happen and willing to share information freely.

clue.text: Marine creatures: see odd shoal swimming about

indicators.note: swimming about means moving around, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An unusual school of fish is seen moving in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooded seals are Arctic seals whose males have an inflatable nasal hood.

clue.text: Swimmer given shelter, getting back

indicators.note: getting back tells us to read the word for shelter in reverse order

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A swimmer is offered cover and recovers.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long fish, so it is a swimmer in a crossword sense.

clue.text: Pizza obtained in San Francisco area?

parts.note: San Francisco is in California, abbreviated Cal
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: Someone asks where in the Bay Area to get a pizza.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that San Francisco gives its state, California, abbreviated CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A calzone is a folded pizza, an Italian turnover of dough with a filling.

clue.text: Dog drinks nothing — has article to eat

indicators.note: to eat means the drinking word takes the other words inside it

parts.note: laps means drinks, as a dog does
taken as written
a is the indefinite article
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dog drinks nothing but has something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' sits at the front, so the surface reads as a pet's routine; the Lhasa apso is a Tibetan breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lhasa apso is a small long-haired Tibetan dog breed.

clue.text: Remove head of rabbit for stew

indicators.note: remove head of tells us to drop the first letter of the word

parts.note: to rabbit (British slang) is to talk on and on, to blather

explanation.surface: A cook's instruction for preparing a rabbit for the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' and 'stew' look like a recipe; but rabbit is the verb, to chatter, and stew is a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a lather or in a stew are both idioms for being worked up and agitated.

clue.text: Break rule, perhaps, in theatre outside the West End

parts.note: the Fringe is alternative theatre, outside mainstream London West End venues

explanation.surface: An avant-garde show breaks convention away from London's main theatres.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's main theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe is to break or violate a rule, the rule being one example of what is broken.

clue.text: Became friends again? Not true

explanation.surface: After a quarrel, a reconciliation is denied.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up is to reconcile, and a made-up story is invented, false.

clue.text: Butler features in unimpressive story

indicators.note: features in means the butler appears inside the other word

parts.note: pale, as in a pale imitation, means weak or unimpressive
Rab Butler was a British Conservative statesman

explanation.surface: A servant stars in a dull tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Butler is the politician R.A. 'Rab' Butler, not a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a simple story told to teach a moral lesson.

clue.text: Drive to place of great beauty bordering south German city

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in street names

indicators.note: bordering means the place of beauty wraps around the letter for south

parts.note: Eden, the garden of Paradise, is a place of great beauty

explanation.surface: A trip to a beautiful spot near a southern German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is the capital of Saxony in eastern Germany, so it is a German city.

clue.text: German man is slimmer?

explanation.surface: A man from Germany is losing weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieter is a common German first name, and a dieter is one trying to slim.

clue.text: It's in hand for woodcutter?

indicators.note: in tells us the first words go inside the word for hand

parts.note: a paw is a hand, informally

explanation.surface: A lumberjack has his tool in his hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitsaw is a long two-handled saw used to cut logs, a tool for woodcutting.

clue.text: Aid injured mount

indicators.note: something injured is damaged, so the word is broken into a new order

explanation.surface: Help is given to a hurt horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ida is a mountain in Greek mythology, on Crete and in Anatolia.

clue.text: Computer program to ascertain bank customer's suitability?

parts.note: to screen is to check something, to ascertain whether it is acceptable
a saver is someone who keeps money in a bank

explanation.surface: Software is used by a bank to vet its clients.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the phrase is to screen a saver, checking a customer's suitability; 'suitability' completes that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen saver is software that shows moving images when a computer is idle.

clue.text: Member of the orchestra is a pansy

explanation.surface: An orchestral player is called a weakling.
explanation.definitionFit: The viola is a string instrument in the orchestra, and violas are flowers of the pansy genus.

clue.text: Brownish colour one noticed in back copies

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for one is placed inside
back tells us to reverse the word for copies

parts.note: to ape is to copy, so apes means copies
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An old photo tint is spotted in back issues of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses APES to SEPA, and I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown pigment, the tone of old photographs.

clue.text: Analysis of an illness

explanation.surface: A diagnosis of a disease is given.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakdown is a detailed itemised analysis, and also a collapse in health, as in nervous breakdown.

clue.text: Fish, I agreed, should be raised here

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: OK means agreed

explanation.surface: A fish farmer agrees fish should be reared here.
explanation.definitionFit: Koi are ornamental carp kept in ponds, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Went quickly round rear of old garden hut?

indicators.note: round means the word for went quickly surrounds the other letter

parts.note: to woosh (whoosh) is to move quickly with a rushing sound

indicators.note: rear of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone hurried round the back of an old shed in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodshed is an outbuilding for storing firewood, a kind of garden hut.

clue.text: Motorway madness is not what it seems

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north–south motorway, written MI
rage is fury, madness

explanation.surface: Road rage on a motorway turns out to be an illusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; crosswords write its figure 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, something that appears real but is not there.
